title: AbbVie Raises 2025 Profit Outlook as Skyrizi, Rinvoq Fuel Strong Growth

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: AbbVie raised its annual profit ​forecast on Friday after topping Wall Street third-quarter expectations, driven by ‌booming demand for its newer immunology and brain disease drugs, sending its shares up 1 percent.

The drugmaker's shares have risen about 27% this year to record highs, as investors expect its newer immunology drugs, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, along with its treatments in development, to offset declining sales of former ⁠marquee drug Humira.

"We are making significant progress across our pipeline," CEO Robert ​Michael told analysts, adding that AbbVie sees several longer-term growth opportunities in ​the 2030s that are not yet reflected in Wall Street forecasts.

AbbVie is advancing several key drug development programs, including lutikizumab, a skin disease drug that could broaden its immunology ​franchise, and ABBV-295, an experimental weight-loss treatment licensed last year from Danish ​biotech Gubra.

IMMUNOLOGY, NEUROSCIENCE DRIVE BEAT

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $17.40 billion and adjusted earnings ‌of $3.82 ⁠per share, with both figures topping analyst estimates.

Skyrizi, indicated for skin and gastrointestinal conditions, recorded sales of $5.78 billion for the quarter, growing 22.7% from a year earlier and beating Wall Street estimates of $5.75 billion, according to data ​compiled by LSEG.

Rinvoq, ​which is used ⁠to treat a range of inflammatory joint, skin and gastrointestinal conditions, generated $2.71 billion in revenue, in line with ​analyst expectations.

AbbVie's neuroscience portfolio also contributed to the earnings ​beat, with ⁠revenue climbing 19% to $3.39 billion, helped by Botox Therapeutic and antipsychotic drug Vraylar.

The drugmaker now expects annual adjusted profit of $13.95 to $13.99 per share, compared with ⁠its prior ​view of $13.76 to $13.96. The forecast includes a ​69 cents hit from acquired in-process R&D and milestone expenses booked year-to-date through the third ​quarter.
